name: root-structure-policy
purpose: Defines root-level directory classes so the workspace can distinguish registered projects, shared operating folders, AI assistant runtime adapters, local-only folders, and generated outputs.

reader_guide.summary: Open this file when deciding whether a root folder should become a project, a shared operations folder, an AI assistant runtime adapter, a private local-only folder, or ignored generated output.
how_to_read: Read directory_classes first to understand the allowed root folder categories.
Use reserved_operational_dirs for tracked shared workspace folders.
Use runtime_adapter_dirs for tracked dot-directories that exist only to adapt shared rules to a specific AI coding tool.
Use local_only_dirs for folders that may exist on disk but must not become durable knowledge sources.
Use project_registry_path to find tracked root projects and ownership boundaries.
Run the structure audit command before and after root-level structure changes.
update_triggers: A new root-level folder category is introduced.
A root-level project is created, archived, or renamed.
A local-only or generated-output folder appears at repository root.
An AI assistant runtime-specific instruction directory is introduced.
Project boundary rules or reserved workspace folders change.
The structure-audit tool reports unknown root folders.

structure_rules.rule: Every tracked non-underscore root directory must be registered in _ops/projects/registry.json unless it is a documented local-only or generated-output directory.
structure_rules.reason: Unregistered root folders make ownership and lifecycle ambiguous.

structure_rules.rule: Reserved operational directories must contain shared workspace assets, not project-specific work that belongs inside a project folder.
structure_rules.reason: Shared folders should reduce repeated work, not hide project ownership.

structure_rules.rule: Local-only directories may exist on disk but must be ignored by git, excluded from generated maps/snapshots, and must not be used as durable source-of-truth for future agents.
structure_rules.reason: Private local scratch state can disappear or contain material that should not be committed, indexed, summarized, or shown to AI by default.

structure_rules.rule: Generated build outputs should stay inside the owning project and be ignored unless the artifact is intentionally committed as a durable deliverable.
structure_rules.reason: Root-level generated output folders become hard to attribute and can confuse project boundaries.

structure_rules.rule: Each registered project's durable top-level directories should be listed in that project registry entry's project_specific_home list unless they match generated_output_dirs.
structure_rules.reason: A maintainer should be able to understand project folder purpose from the registry without inspecting every file.

structure_rules.rule: Runtime adapter directories must contain only thin tool-specific files that point back to shared operating principles, not independent policy forks.
structure_rules.reason: The workspace should remain usable from Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, or another tool without duplicating and drifting core rules.

structure_rules.rule: Run the structure audit before and after root-level folder changes, project creation, archive moves, or reserved-folder changes.
structure_rules.reason: A deterministic check catches ambiguous folders before they become long-lived conventions.

field_guide.meaning: Path to the source-of-truth registry for tracked root projects.
Allowed conceptual categories for root-level directories.
Human-facing grouping of root folders into project plane, operations control plane, knowledge plane, runtime adapter plane, protected local plane, and generated local plane.
Tracked underscore-prefixed folders for shared workspace operations and knowledge.
Root folders that may exist locally but must stay ignored and non-authoritative.
Tracked root dot-directories used only to adapt shared workspace rules to specific AI coding tools.
Known generated or dependency directories that should stay project-local and ignored.
Deterministic command for checking root structure against this policy.

logical_architecture_layers.purpose: Independently owned root projects with their own lifecycle, commands, README, docs, tests, and artifacts.
logical_architecture_layers.rule: Add a new root project only when the concern has independent ownership or lifecycle; register it in _ops/projects/registry.json.

logical_architecture_layers.purpose: Shared execution control, policies, requirements, specs, history, coordination, workflows, prompts, maps, and evaluations.
logical_architecture_layers.rule: These folders are shared platform control surfaces, not project-specific storage.

logical_architecture_layers.purpose: Reusable knowledge, philosophy, templates, tools, skills, research, and archived projects.
logical_architecture_layers.rule: Promote project-local assets here only when they are reusable across projects.

logical_architecture_layers.purpose: Thin adapters for specific AI coding tools that point back to shared operating principles.
logical_architecture_layers.rule: Do not fork policy here; keep adapters thin.

logical_architecture_layers.purpose: Local-only sensitive or private material that exists on disk but is not durable repository knowledge.
logical_architecture_layers.rule: Do not read, index, summarize, or use contents by default. Route real sensitive files to _private/sensitive/ or an external secret manager.

logical_architecture_layers.purpose: Transient local output that is not a durable artifact until moved into the owning project artifacts folder.
logical_architecture_layers.rule: Do not treat root outputs as final deliverables.

directory_classes.description: Root project with its own purpose, lifecycle, README, commands, and project registry entry.
Tracked underscore-prefixed shared workspace folder for cross-project rules, operations, templates, tools, research, or history.
Tracked root dot-directory for AI assistant-specific instruction/rule adapters that reference the shared operating model.
Ignored private or scratch folder that can exist locally but is not durable repository state.
Ignored build output, dependency cache, or generated runtime state owned by a project.
